requirement:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.
#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.
**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Getting the stack trace.** Console output truncates the exception to its message; `-p:ErrorLog=out.sarif` preserves the full description, including the stack trace and an `ISymbol:` context line naming the offending type:

```
dotnet build -p:ErrorLog=out.sarif
```

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

[mp-repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/30408133/mp-repro.zip)

story.summary: Fixes the crash when a [MessagePackObject] type has a member whose type is a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly. The change has three parts. First, one diagnostic site now uses `DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()` where it used to index `[0]` (line 1077). Second, a second site now goes through a new null-safe helper, `GetPropertyIdentifierLocation` (line 985). Third, the analyzer's diagnostic sink is wrapped so that any diagnostic not located in a syntax tree of the current compilation is silently dropped. Three tests compile a defining assembly to a metadata-only image and assert two things: the usage project gets no diagnostics, and the resolver source is generated. The change also adds doc paragraphs to README.md and MsgPack004.md.
story.why: Metadata symbols have an empty `DeclaringSyntaxReferences` collection, so indexing `[0]` threw `IndexOutOfRangeException`. The MemberNeedsKey diagnostic at line 1077 is built even when no reporter is set, which explains the generator crash (CS8785). That crash meant no resolver was emitted.
touches_beyond_requirement: Line 239 plus lines 1436-1450: the analyzer now drops every diagnostic that has no in-source location in the current compilation. This includes diagnostics previously reported at Location.None, so the reach is wider than the metadata case.
README.md and doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md document the new suppression policy: problems in referenced types must be fixed in the defining project.
The UnkeyedMember test locks in that suppression as expected behaviour.
story.confidence_overview: I am fairly confident about the core fix at line 1077 and the repro tests. I am less confident that no other `[0]` site remains, because the issue names line 735 and the diff does not visibly touch it. The diagnostic filter is a design decision with broader effects than the bug, and the owner should judge it.

refusals.what: The analyzer's reporter is wrapped to drop any diagnostic not located in the current compilation, including Location.None diagnostics.
refusals.why: This behaviour change goes beyond the crash fix and can hide diagnostics users previously saw. Whether that trade-off is acceptable is a maintainer decision.

refusals.what: The UnkeyedMember test asserts that the consumer sees no MemberNeedsKey diagnostic for a referenced type with an unkeyed public member.
refusals.why: The test encodes the new suppression policy as correct, rather than only checking for absence of a crash.

refusals.what: User-facing docs commit to a diagnostic-reporting policy for referenced assemblies.
refusals.why: These docs were not requested. They describe user-visible analyzer behaviour chosen by the agent.

findings.description: Claim C6 disputed: ClosedGenericRecordStruct_FromMetadataReference does not reproduce the issue's Lib/App repro verbatim: lines 575-576 of GenericsFormatterTests.cs add an explicit [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial class AppResolver { } (and line 579 asserts App.AppResolver.g.cs), whereas the issue's app repro has no [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] declaration and relies on the implicit default GeneratedMessagePackResolver. Lines 575-576 are also changed lines inside the citation that the claim does not describe.

The filter drops every diagnostic whose location is not in source, including Location.None. Several existing sites pass locations from helpers like GetIdentifierLocation/GetLocation that can be null. Diagnostics the analyzer used to emit with no location are now silently swallowed. That includes consumer-relevant problems about referenced types, e.g. a metadata type that is not formattable. Roslyn only forbids locations in trees outside the compilation; Location.None is allowed.

The issue names three `[0]` sites (735, 1009, 1101 in 3.1.8). The diff changes two. Nothing visible shows the third (line ~735) was fixed or is unreachable, and no test exercises the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull path at line 985 with a metadata type.

The docs say diagnostics are reported by the defining assembly. That only holds if the defining project itself runs the MessagePack analyzer. A NuGet package built without it can ship unkeyed members, and consumers now get no warning at all.

GetPropertyIdentifierLocation casts property.DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?.GetSyntax() as PropertyDeclarationSyntax. For a positional record or record struct declared in source in the current compilation (e.g. [MessagePackObject] public partial record R([property: Key((string?)null)] string Name)), the synthesized IPropertySymbol's syntax node is a ParameterSyntax, not a PropertyDeclarationSyntax, so GetPropertyIdentifierLocation returns null. BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull (line 985) is then created with Location.None and silently dropped by ReportIfLocatedInCompilation (line 1446) even though the offending declaration is in the compilation being analyzed.

out_of_scope.description: The global diagnostic filter (line 239, 1436-1450) changes which diagnostics every analyzer path reports. The crash fix only needed null-safe location lookups.
New documentation section describing the suppression policy for referenced-assembly types.
New documentation section describing the analyzer's reporting scope.
